offence_severity: Minimum 6 months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000/-
physical_harm: The victim was in the grip of the appellant-accused who was pulling her towards his chest to embrace her, causing her to try to push him back
number_of_offences: Multiple charges were filed, but the conviction was upheld under Section 354 of the IPC
premeditation_planning: The court inferred culpable intention from the sequence of events
key_evidence_accepted: The court accepted the testimony of PW-13 (Ms. Aradhana), who witnessed the incident, and found her deposition reliable and corroborative with other prosecution witnesses. The court also accepted the sequence of events leading to the molestation as sufficient to establish the essential ingredients of Section 354 of the IPC.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly PW-13, as truthful, consistent, and inspiring confidence. The court found her testimony reliable and corroborative with other prosecution witnesses.
bail_history: The appellant-accused was granted bail by this Court by its order dated 11.11.2010.
trial_duration: The trial started with the FIR registered on 516 of 1999, charge sheet filed on 16.11.2000, trial judgment on 21.12.2009, and the Supreme Court decision on 23 September 2016.
legal_representation: K.V. Viswanathan, Sr. Adv., Ms. Priyanjali Singh, Dhananjay Ray, Mehul M. Gupta, Advs. for the Appellant. Ms. Vibha Datta Makhija, Sr. Adv., Rajiv Nanda, Ajay Sharma, B. V. Bairam Das, Arvind Kumar Sharma, Vikas Mehta, Ms. Anushree Menon, Advs. for the Respondents.
investigation_status: FIR registered on 516 of 1999, charge sheet filed on 16.11.2000, investigation completed and case registered, trial completed, and appeal decided by the Supreme Court.

appeal_history.trial_court: The appellant-accused was convicted and sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for six months along with a fine of Rs. 1,000/-.
appeal_history.high_court: The High Court dismissed the revision filed by the appellant-accused on 01.09.2010 and upheld the sentence.
appeal_history.supreme_court: The Supreme Court confirmed the conviction under Section 354 of the IPC and modified the sentence to the period already undergone by the appellant-accused.

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant-accused, a senior police officer, molested a minor girl, and the victim's testimony was reliable and corroborative. The delay in reporting the incident was explained as due to the victim's embarrassment and societal pressures, making it condonable. The evidence of the eye witness (PW-13) was sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused.
defence_argument: The defence contended that the prosecution's story was false and frivolous, and the appellant-accused was framed by the complainant and high-level officers. They argued that the signature on the Memorandum was forged, the delay in reporting was not explained properly, and the absence of certain witnesses cast doubt on the prosecution's case.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that knowledge or intention to outrage a woman's modesty is an essential ingredient of the offence under Section 354 IPC, which can be inferred from the circumstances of the case rather than direct evidence.
precedent_relied_upon: Vidyadharan vs. State of Kerala (2004) 1 SCC 215; Tarkeshwar Sahu vs. State of Bihar (2006) 8 SCC 560; Mobarik Ali Ahmed vs. The State of Bombay AIR 1957 SC 857; Smt. Bhagwan Kaur vs. Shri Maharaj Krishan Sharma & Ors. (1973) 4 SCC 46
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed after considering mitigating factors such as the appellant's old age, health ailments, and responsibility for his daughter, and the court decided to reduce the sentence to the period already undergone due to his advanced age.
judicial_mitigating_factors: Old age of the appellant-accused, health ailments, responsibility of looking after the unmarried daughter suffering from congenital heart disease, past meritorious service, and prolonged trial.
